prior_importants.description: `commitsPastPin` now rethrows `RewrittenGitDirError`. `recordMerge` calls it before `appendEvent(db, session.id, 'merge', …)`. So a main `.git` rewritten after the fast-forward lands means the `merge` event is never written, even though the session is already `merged` and the target already holds the sha.

findings.description: The refusal `recordMerge` rethrows after the fast-forward is bare: `RewrittenGitDirError`'s text says 'Refusing to run git ... treat the session that wrote it as compromised' and nothing about the merge. Trigger: the new test's scenario (commondir planted during the teardown, local mode). `pup merge` exits through `refuseScrubbed` with only that text, while `main` already holds the session's sha, the session is `merged`, and the ratchet and decision draft were skipped; the other refusals on this path say 'nothing was merged'. Suggest extending the message before `throw refused`, as `withLedgerKept` does (e.g. 'The merge of <sha> into <target> had already landed and is recorded; the ratchet and decision draft did not run.').

The new `recordMerge` JSDoc says "A main `.git` rewritten after the fast-forward refuses that count", but the code catches any error from `commitsPastPin`, writes the event without `leftBehind`, and rethrows the original. A reader would not learn that any failure of the count still records the merge. Suggested shape: "If the count throws, the event is still written without it, since the target already holds `sha`, and the error is rethrown."

The test comment says "The window ADR 0172 names: the fast-forward landed and the session, not yet killed, rewrites `.git`…", but ADR 0172 names no teardown-specific window (L100-101 only says a mid-gate plant is refused at the next read). Drop the ADR attribution, e.g. "Planted from `killSession`: the fast-forward has landed, but the session is still alive to rewrite `.git`."
